LIBRARIAN: Hello, can I help you?
STUDENT: Yes, I'd like to join the library, please. I've just moved to the area.
LIBRARIAN: Welcome! I just need to fill in this form. What's your first name?
STUDENT: Mei.
LIBRARIAN: And your surname?
STUDENT: Lin. L-I-N.
LIBRARIAN: Thank you. And your address?
STUDENT: Flat 3, 58 Harbour View, Portwell.
LIBRARIAN: Was that 58 or 68?
STUDENT: Fifty-eight. Five, eight.
LIBRARIAN: And the postcode?
STUDENT: P-W-2, 6-J-N.
LIBRARIAN: So that's PW2 6JN. Can I see something with your address on it?
STUDENT: I have a letter from my bank. Is that OK?
LIBRARIAN: That's perfect. Now, with your card you can borrow up to 12 books at a time, for three weeks.
STUDENT: Can I borrow DVDs as well?
LIBRARIAN: Yes, but DVDs are one pound each. Books are free.
STUDENT: OK. When are you open?
LIBRARIAN: Monday to Saturday, nine till six. We're closed on Sundays. And on Wednesdays we close early, at one o'clock.
STUDENT: Wednesday, one o'clock. Do you have computers?
LIBRARIAN: Yes, upstairs. You can use them for free for one hour a day. You just need to book at the desk.
STUDENT: Great. Are there any clubs?
LIBRARIAN: There's a reading group on Thursday evenings, and a conversation club for people learning English on Fridays.
STUDENT: Oh, the conversation club sounds good.
LIBRARIAN: It's very friendly. Here's your card. Please write your name on the back.
STUDENT: Thank you very much.

Address: Flat 3, (2) ______ Harbour View, Portwell
Proof of address: letter from (3) ______
Maximum number of books: (4) ______
Early closing day: (5) ______
question: Complete the form. Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER for answer (1).
explanation: L-I-N と つづりを 言っている。Mei は 名（first name）。

RECEPTIONIST: Brookside Dental Practice, good morning.
PATIENT: Hello. I'd like to register as a new patient, please.
RECEPTIONIST: Of course. Can I start with your full name?
PATIENT: Georgia Thwaite. That's T-H-W-A-I-T-E.
RECEPTIONIST: Thanks. Date of birth?
PATIENT: The 30th of November, 1988.
RECEPTIONIST: And your address?
PATIENT: 112 Fenwick Avenue, Castleford.
RECEPTIONIST: Lovely. Are you registered with a dentist at the moment?
PATIENT: I was, in Manchester, but I moved here in the summer for a new job.
RECEPTIONIST: OK. And what do you do, just for our records?
PATIENT: I'm a pharmacist.
RECEPTIONIST: Fine. Are you taking any medication?
PATIENT: Just something for hay fever in the spring, nothing else.
RECEPTIONIST: Noted. Is there any particular reason you'd like to come in? Pain, for instance?
PATIENT: Not pain exactly, but one of my back teeth is sensitive when I drink anything cold.
RECEPTIONIST: Right. So I'll book you a check-up, and the dentist can look at that. The earliest is Tuesday the 8th at quarter past two.
PATIENT: I'm working then. Anything in the morning?
RECEPTIONIST: Wednesday the 9th at ten to nine?
PATIENT: That's ideal, before work.
RECEPTIONIST: Great. A check-up costs £26 and you pay on the day. Which dentist would you prefer? We have Dr Shah and Dr Morgan.
PATIENT: I don't mind.
RECEPTIONIST: I'll put you with Dr Shah, then. Please arrive ten minutes early to fill in a health questionnaire.
PATIENT: Will do. Thank you.

Surname: (1) ______
Occupation: (2) ______
Medication: for hay (3) ______
Appointment: Wednesday 9th at (4) ______ to nine
Cost of check-up: £(5) ______
question: Complete the form. Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER for answer (1).
explanation: T-H-W-A-I-T-E と つづりを 言っている。

passage:
OFFICER: Hello, Southern Cross Homestay Services, Melbourne. Jess speaking.
STUDENT: Hi, I'm calling from Japan. I'm going to study English in Melbourne next year and I'd like to apply for a homestay.
OFFICER: Great! Let's start with your name.
STUDENT: Kenta Morishita. M-O-R-I-S-H-I-T-A.
OFFICER: Thanks, Kenta. And which language school will you attend?
STUDENT: Bayside English Academy.
OFFICER: When does your course start?
STUDENT: On the 15th of January. I'll arrive two days before, on the 13th.
OFFICER: How long would you like to stay with a family?
STUDENT: My course is twenty weeks, but I'd like to try homestay for the first 12 weeks and then maybe move into a flat with friends.
OFFICER: That's very common. Now, any preferences about the family? Children, pets?
STUDENT: I don't mind children. But I'm allergic to cats, so no cats, please. A dog would be fine.
OFFICER: I'll note that down. Do you have any special diet?
STUDENT: Not really. I eat everything except seafood. I don't like it at all.
OFFICER: OK. And what are your hobbies? We try to match students with families who share their interests.
STUDENT: I play the guitar, and I really enjoy cycling.
OFFICER: Lovely. The fee is three hundred and ten Australian dollars a week, which includes breakfast and dinner every day, and lunch at weekends.
STUDENT: And is there a placement fee?
OFFICER: Yes, a one-off fee of two hundred and fifty dollars. Would you also like us to meet you at the airport? That's an extra hundred and five dollars.
STUDENT: Yes, please. My English isn't very confident yet.
OFFICER: No problem at all. I'll email you the forms today.

[Form]
Surname: (1) ______
Length of homestay: (2) ______ weeks
Allergy: (3) ______
Does not eat: (4) ______
Hobbies: guitar and (5) ______
question: Complete the form. Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER for answer (1).
explanation: M-O-R-I-S-H-I-T-A と つづりを 言っている。

BOX OFFICE: Riverside Playhouse box office, how can I help?
CALLER: Hello, I'm booking for a group from our walking club. We'd like to see "The Lighthouse Keeper" next month.
BOX OFFICE: Lovely choice. Which performance?
CALLER: We were thinking of an evening show, but several members don't like driving in the dark, so the matinee on Saturday the 17th, please.
BOX OFFICE: That starts at half past two. How many tickets?
CALLER: 18, please.
BOX OFFICE: Groups of fifteen or more get a discount, so instead of £26 each, they're £21.
CALLER: Excellent. Where would we be sitting?
BOX OFFICE: For a group that size, the best seats left together are in the circle, rows C and D.
CALLER: Is there a lift up to the circle? Two of our members use walking sticks.
BOX OFFICE: Yes, there's a lift by the main entrance. I can also make sure they're on the end of a row.
CALLER: That would be very kind. And could we pre-order drinks for the interval?
BOX OFFICE: Certainly. We'll have them waiting at the bar. Shall I take the name for the booking?
CALLER: It's Hilary Featherstone. F-E-A-T-H-E-R-S-T-O-N-E.
BOX OFFICE: Thank you, Ms Featherstone. How would you like to receive the tickets? We can post them, or you can collect them on the day.
CALLER: Collect them on the day, please. It's easier than sending them to everyone.
BOX OFFICE: Then please come to the box office at least thirty minutes before the start.
CALLER: Will do. Is there a car park?
BOX OFFICE: The nearest is on Quay Street. It's eight pounds for the afternoon, but if you show your theatre tickets, you'll get a twenty per cent reduction.
CALLER: Perfect. Thanks so much.

CALLER: OK. Is it furnished?

AGENT: One undercover space. Also, there's a secure storage cage for bikes.
CALLER: Brilliant, I cycle to work. When is it available from?
AGENT: From the 1st of February.
CALLER: Could I see it this week?
AGENT: We have an inspection on Thursday at five thirty. Or Saturday at eleven.
CALLER: Thursday is difficult. Saturday, please.
AGENT: OK. What's your name?
CALLER: Aroha Tipene. That's T-I-P-E-N-E.
AGENT: And how long a lease are you looking for?
CALLER: Six months, initially.
AGENT: The owner prefers twelve months, I'm afraid. Would that be a problem?
CALLER: No, 12 months is fine.
AGENT: Good. If you decide to apply, you'll need to pay a bond of four weeks' rent, and you'll need references from your previous landlord and your employer.
CALLER: Understood. Are pets allowed? I have a rabbit.
AGENT: Small pets are fine with permission, so a rabbit should be OK.
CALLER: Wonderful. See you on Saturday.
